input: Assess the credit and counterparty risk of AMC Entertainment

financials.metric: Total corporate borrowings (current maturities plus long-term corporate borrowings)
financials.stated_by: AMC Entertainment Holdings, Inc. (Form 10-Q; calculated as $148.9m current maturities plus $3,702.7m long-term corporate borrowings)

financials.period: As of 2026-06-30; assessment through the next twelve months
financials.stated_by: AMC management stated that existing cash and cash generated from operations should be sufficient to fund operations and satisfy obligations through the next twelve months; no dollar liquidity total was stated

credit_ratings.summary: Fitch assigned AMC a first-time Long-Term Issuer Default Rating of B- with a Positive Outlook; first-lien senior notes were B- / RR4, the senior secured term loan B / RR3, and Muvico exchangeable notes CCC / RR6.

S&P assigned B+ / recovery 1 to the proposed $850m first-lien term loan and $2bn first-lien notes due 2031, CCC / recovery 6 to the proposed $1.12bn second-lien term loan due 2033, upgraded the $116m second-lien exchangeable notes due 2030 to B- from CCC, and said the B- issuer rating and Stable outlook were unchanged.
S&P upgraded AMC's issuer credit rating to B- from CCC+ and maintained a Stable outlook, citing improved operating performance and an expected path to sustained positive reported free cash flow.

debt_events.summary: AMC completed a $3.97bn refinancing: $2.0bn first-lien notes due 2031, an $850m first-lien term loan, and a $1.12bn second-lien term loan due 2033. It used proceeds and cash on hand to tender for existing 7.5% secured notes, redeem remaining notes in February 2027, redeem Muvico's $903.4m notes due 2029, and repay AMC and Odeon term loans; approximately 98.8% of the AMC secured notes were tendered.
AMC stated it was in full compliance with all agreements, including related covenants, governing its outstanding debt as of June 30, 2026.

Holders voluntarily exchanged all $155.845562m of Muvico New Exchangeable Notes outstanding for 142,102,295 AMC common shares plus accrued interest; the notes were canceled and AMC recorded a $33.0m loss on extinguishment.
Odeon Finco borrowed $425m of new term loans maturing in 2031 and used the proceeds plus about $38.2m of cash to redeem Odeon notes due 2027 and related costs, including about $23.5m of interest.
Reuters reported that AMC reached a deal with some creditors, including Odeon creditors, to clear the path for debt refinancing intended to cut interest payments and extend maturities.

distress_signals.summary: AMC's Form 10-Q said historical cash-burn rates were not sustainable long term and warned that, if it cannot obtain sufficient additional liquidity beyond twelve months, it likely would seek an in-court or out-of-court restructuring of liabilities; this is risk language, not a bankruptcy filing or stated default.

Fitch described negative free cash flow, high cash-interest burden and a complex capital structure; it reported LTM EBITDA leverage of 6.5x and said AMC had a sizable 2029/2030 maturity wall. Fitch also noted AMC had closed underperforming theatres as part of portfolio optimization.
Reuters reported that AMC forecast a $127.4m fourth-quarter loss, which would have been its ninth consecutive quarterly loss, amid pandemic-era debt and uneven box-office recovery.

ownership.value: Public company; AMC Entertainment Holdings, Inc. is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under ticker AMC. No recent change of control or sponsor was verified.

output.risk_rationale: AMC's ability to pay is improving but remains materially leveraged: the June 30, 2026 Form 10-Q reported $778.4m of cash, $3.85bn of corporate borrowings, Q2 revenue of $1.60bn and operating income of $238.1m, while management cautioned that long-term cash burn was not sustainable and that insufficient future liquidity could lead to restructuring [SEC 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1411579/000141157926000059/amc-20260630x10q.htm). The October 5 refinancing materially extended maturities to 2031/2033 and S&P upgraded the issuer to B-/Stable, but Fitch still described negative FCF, 6.5x LTM EBITDA leverage, high interest burden and a 2029/2030 maturity wall; that combination supports an elevated rather than low or moderate counterparty-risk assessment [AMC refinancing](https://investor.amctheatres.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/443/amc-entertainment-holdings-inc-announces-results-of-tender-offer-the-closing-of-first-lien-notes-offering-and-new-term-loan-facilities-totaling-a-3-97-billion-refinancing-of-existing-debt) [Fitch](https://www.fitchratings.com/research/corporate-finance/fitch-assigns-amc-entertainment-first-time-b-idr-outlook-positive-08-09-2026) [S&P](https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/sourceId/101697301).
